subject.title: Gateway should expose HTTP REST endpoints for common queries

question: Should trusted admin HTTP RPC expose read-only session query methods such as `sessions.list` and `sessions.get`, or should HTTP session-data access wait for a narrower session API design?
rationale: The code path is clear, but the remaining choice is an operator/security boundary and public API shape decision for session state over HTTP.

options.title: Extend admin HTTP RPC
options.body: Add only the maintainer-approved read-only session query methods to the existing default-off trusted admin HTTP RPC allowlist with docs and tests.

options.title: Canonicalize under broader session API work
options.body: Keep this issue open only as linked context and make https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/20934 own the full session-management HTTP API shape.

options.title: Keep WebSocket-only for session state
options.body: Leave session list/detail off HTTP and document that integrations needing session state must use Gateway WebSocket RPC.

recommendation.title: Extend admin HTTP RPC
recommendation.body: Add only the maintainer-approved read-only session query methods to the existing default-off trusted admin HTTP RPC allowlist with docs and tests.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main blame ties the admin HTTP RPC allowlist and session handler surfaces to this owner signal.
